brief: ING's September US jobs read: nonfarm payrolls rose only 29k versus a 90k consensus, with 60k of downward revisions, pushing the unemployment rate to 4.2% from 4.1% as the participation rate partially recovered. Wage growth cooled to 3% year-on-year from 3.1%, which ING reads as no inflation threat from the labour market. Manufacturing was the bright spot, rising for a fourth straight month (72k cumulative since the start of the year), aided by strong advanced-manufacturing surveys; construction also rose, tied to data-centre activity. Services weakened: information, financial, professional-business-services and government payrolls all fell. The labour force grew 485k, lifting participation to 61.8% from 61.6%, and the unemployed-to-vacancy ratio has normalized toward parity from two vacancies per unemployed worker in early 2022, with a low quits rate pointing to further wage-growth downside. Comments from the NY Fed's Williams and Vice Chair Jefferson suggest no urgency to hike, so Fed leadership leans toward an October hold; a hot 14 October CPI print is the swing factor. ING's call: December remains the likely next hike, and market pricing of 3-4 hikes is too aggressive.
